short: A period of religious turbulence under the brief reigns of Edward VI and Mary I.
full: The mid-Tudor period was characterised by rapid swings in religious policy. The boy-king Edward VI pushed England towards radical Protestantism, while his half-sister Mary I vehemently attempted to restore Catholicism, earning the moniker 'Bloody Mary' for her persecution of Protestants. It was a time of social unrest and economic difficulty.
